name: Apple, Inc.
summary:
Apple (AAPL) reported earnings of $1.91 per share on revenue of $109.42 billion for the fiscal third quarter ended June 2026. The consensus earnings estimate was $1.88 per share on revenue of $108.79 billion. The Earnings Whisper number was $1.97 per share. The company missed expectations by 3.05% while revenue grew 16.36% on a year-over-year basis.

The company said during its conference call it expects fourth-quarter earnings of $1.91 to $2.04 per share on revenue of $111.69 billion to $113.74 billion. The current consensus earnings estimate is $2.03 per share on revenue of $115.78 billion for the quarter ending September 30, 2026.

“Today, Apple is proud to report our strongest June quarter ever, with double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services, and in every geographic segment,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. “At WWDC26, we were thrilled to introduce the all-new Siri AI, alongside all of Apple’s latest software innovations and important new child safety features.”

Apple Inc designs, manufactures, & markets mobile communication & media devices, personal computers, & portable digital music players, & sells a variety of related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, & third-party digital content.
subject: Apple Missed Expectations

subject: MasTec Missed Expectations

name: Amazon.com, Inc.
summary:
Amazon.com (AMZN) reported earnings of $1.88 per share on revenue of $200.61 billion for the second quarter ended June 2026. The consensus earnings estimate was $1.83 per share on revenue of $196.85 billion. The Earnings Whisper number was $1.87 per share. The company beat expectations by 0.53% while revenue grew 19.62% on a year-over-year basis.

The company said it expects third quarter revenue of $197.0 billion to $202.0 billion. The current consensus revenue estimate is $204.30 billion for the quarter ending September 30, 2026.

“AWS is booming, growing 36.7% year-over-year in Q2—our fastest growth in 18 quarters—and our AI and Chips businesses each eclipsed run rates of more than $25 billion,” said Andy Jassy, President and CEO, Amazon. “In Stores, we again set record delivery speeds for Prime members in the first half of the year—over 40% more items delivered same-day or overnight, with Grocery and Everyday Essentials growing meaningfully faster than the rest of the business. And, Advertising had another strong quarter with 26% year-over-year growth. There’s a lot to be excited about, and we have much more coming for customers in the second half of the year and beyond.”

Amazon.com Inc is an online retailer. The Company sells its products through the website which provides services, such as advertising services and co-branded credit card agreements. It also offers electronic devices like Kindle e-readers and Fire tablets.
subject: Amazon.com Beat Expectations
